contract: Pure, bounded trailing-edge latest-binary-value policy for one caller-owned partition: host supplies a UTF-8 epoch, quiet interval, nondecreasing samples in a nonnegative monotonic origin and timer delivery. State starts with no last sample; accepted puts and timeouts, including ignored well-formed nonmatching tokens, record now. Clear preserves last time and generation. Generation maximum is reachable and usable; malformed tokens reject unchanged and well-formed nonmatching tokens are ignored. Matching due timeout emits the latest value once; early matching timeout reschedules at the same deadline. Accepted empty-state and post-emission duplicate timeouts emit and schedule nothing but still record now. No timer, registry, persistence, leading edge or maximum wait.
limits: Timer delivery is not exact and best-effort cancellation is not a correctness guarantee.
State is volatile and caller-owned; no timer, process, registry or store is supplied.
Continuous puts may defer emission indefinitely; there is no leading edge or maximum wait.

grounding.claim: The shared ignored-timeout decision returns no emission; token-branch selection is covered by finite tests.
The completion helper emits its pending value; the latest-put sequence is covered by finite tests.
The selected transition after completion ignores the cleared generation; finite tests exercise duplicate delivery.
The refusal helper retains its exact state; public refusal mapping is covered by finite tests.
The pinned Cure compiler checks the typed production transition and selected law signatures.
Named scenarios cover normal/empty states, serialized order, clear, stale and duplicate delivery, bounded inputs, overflow, generation exhaustion and unchanged-state refusals.
A temporary stale-token boundary bypass is rejected by the stale-generation scenario; the mutation is restored before delivery.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler and runtime representation.
Relies on pinned Elixir binary, UTF-8 validation and public Process API behavior.
The example relies on OTP timer message delivery and monotonic-time behavior.
The caller serializes commands per partition, supplies nondecreasing samples in a nonnegative monotonic origin, owns timer delivery and changes epochs across resets.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable without a running lifecycle; the invoking Unit or Assembly owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Epoch and quiet_ms are validated construction-time inputs; state has no hot reconfiguration API.

control.contract: No runtime lifecycle to pause, drain or resume.
